dimensions.reasons: The submitted scene clearly shows the requested horizontal-axis wind turbine on open grass: a tall tapered white tower, closed nacelle, rounded hub, and exactly three long blades. Group B preview_06 also presents the intended dusk-like outdoor storyboard shot with airborne leaf/debris particles, while drivetrain_raw visibly supports the requested internal machinery.
issues: No time-ordered animation frames demonstrate that the rotor actually spins or that the debris is falling under gravity rather than being statically placed.
The two parallel gray strips leading from the base are visually prominent but do not have a clear requested role in the scene.

dimensions.reasons: Across the Group A wide and detail views, the tower is firmly seated on a circular/faceted foundation, the nacelle is mounted coherently on the tower top, and the hub and all blades visibly join into the rotor assembly. Group B drivetrain_raw shows machinery placed on a substantial internal tray with mounts, housings, and routed cable-like lines rather than disconnected floating pieces.
issues: The gray ground strips appear slightly raised or embedded inconsistently in different wide views, making their physical purpose and contact with the terrain unclear.
Static images do not provide evidence that the particle system's gravity, wind, and turbulence behavior is physically convincing over time.

dimensions.reasons: The turbine is independently recognizable from every major angle: the tapered tower, aerodynamic tapered blades, round hub, and elongated nacelle have clear turbine silhouettes. The white exterior with red-orange blade tips reads well, and Group B drivetrain_raw uses distinct teal, orange, dark metallic, and white components to make the gearbox/generator assembly legible.
issues: The nacelle remains somewhat boxy and faceted compared with a more refined production turbine enclosure.
The saturated teal and orange interior machinery is illustrative rather than especially industrially naturalistic.

dimensions.reasons: Group B preview_04 and preview_06 produce a coherent dusk landscape with a convincing large isolated turbine silhouette, grass foreground, clouded sky, and windblown flecks. The detailed nacelle has panel seams and roof equipment, and the drivetrain close-up has modeled cooling ribs, couplings, mounts, and cables rather than generic blocks.
issues: The grassy terrain has visibly patchy, roughly bounded instance-density regions and relatively uniform underlying green ground.
Several Group A overview renders are noticeably soft, hazy, and low contrast, which weakens distant terrain and fine hardware definition.
The turbine exterior is very clean and uniform, with limited weathering, dirt, or surface variation for an exposed utility-scale structure.

dimensions.reasons: The primary spatial relationships are correct in Group A wide_front, wide_back, and wide_iso: the nacelle is centered atop the tower, the rotor projects from its front, and the three blades are arranged at approximately 120 degrees. The turbine is isolated in a broad open grass landscape, and the Group B storyboard previews use a sensible distant, slightly low ground-level composition to establish scale.
issues: The parallel strips/lines create an unexplained foreground-leading element that competes with the otherwise simple open-field composition.
Actual yaw movement is not demonstrated by a sequence of rendered frames.

dimensions.reasons: The wide views convey a credible utility-scale relationship: the tower is approximately twice a blade radius in visible height, consistent with an approximately 80 m hub and 40 m blades. The nacelle is compact relative to the tower and rotor, the tower narrows upward, and the foundation/access hatch read at a plausible small scale at ground level.
issues: Exact specified base and top tower diameters cannot be verified from the submitted image views.
The rotor can appear somewhat slender and visually light in the hazier overview shots.

dimensions.reasons: The author preview images, especially Group B preview_04 through preview_06, show dusk-appropriate lavender, orange, and dark-storm sky variants with coherent illumination on the white turbine. Exterior panel seams, subtle blade-root rings, red tips, grass, and the colored metallic/plastic-like drivetrain materials provide useful material separation.
issues: Lighting is often diffuse and washed out in the Group A renders, reducing form contrast on the white nacelle and blades.
The external white tower, nacelle, and blades have very similar clean matte/gloss responses, so their material distinctions are modest.
Shadows on the open ground are weak and do not strongly anchor the turbine in the more softly lit views.

dimensions.reasons: The required visible structural inventory is substantially present: one tapered tower and base, one nacelle with yaw-ring-like support, one three-bladed rotor, grass terrain, red blade tips, roof instrumentation, and base access detail. Group B drivetrain_raw additionally shows a deliberate interior assembly including a large finned generator-like cylinder, gearbox-like unit, shafts/collars, coupling/brake-like part, mounting tray, and cables. Group B preview_05 and preview_06 visibly include airborne leaf-like debris and dust-like foreground blur.
issues: There is no Group C motion sequence or other unambiguous evidence proving rotor rotation, wind/turbulence-driven motion, or gravity-driven falling behavior.
The individual main shaft, high-speed shaft, and brake cannot each be identified with certainty from the exposed drivetrain view.
Dust is less clearly defined than the leaf-like debris in the previews.

criteria.criterion: The coherent horizontal-axis turbine uses the specified tapered tubular tower and principal dimensions.
The nacelle is genuinely configured as yaw-capable on the tower.
The nacelle contains every named internal machine arranged as one plausible drivetrain.
The hub carries the complete dimensioned three-blade rotor.
The completed authored scene has believable relative scale and consistently estimated unspecified dimensions.
The final render uses readable and believable material distinctions without prescribing unique materials for fixed object or effect classes.
criteria.evidence: In the author render preview_06, the turbine reads as smooth pale painted/composite material against dense matte green grass and a strongly differentiated dusk sky; orange-red blade tips and dark/orange airborne debris provide additional distinct surface/color treatment. The close drivetrain export also visibly differentiates painted white housing panels, dark base/cables, teal machinery, and a ribbed orange metal-like generator.

criteria.criterion: Enabled Wind and Turbulence fields participate in a functioning rotor-driving setup.
The atmospheric system produces distinct leaves and dust with the complete requested gravity, Wind, and Turbulence behavior.
The complete final lighting system combines a genuine dusk HDRI with exactly one contributing Sun lamp and visibly produces dusk illumination.
The selected storyboard render coherently presents the open-field turbine from the requested camera with effective depth of field and motion blur.
The requested final render and retained editable .blend form one valid Cycles-configured project outcome.

notes: This is a strong, recognizable wind-turbine storyboard scene with credible large-scale proportions, a complete three-blade silhouette, open grass setting, dusk preview variants, and unusually useful modeled drivetrain detail. The principal limitations are soft/washed-out overview presentation, somewhat stylized terrain and materials, and the lack of time-ordered evidence for the requested rotor and particle simulation behavior.
score_policy: Frozen paper score: uncapped 0.5 rubric + 0.5 dimension.
